capitals.note: The page says Vienna 'was made into the capital of the Allobrogian civitas' (undated) and that after the revolt of 61 BC the chieftains 'moved their residence to Vienna'; Solonion is the 'chief town' destroyed in 61. The seat before 121 is not dated (confidence 1).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Allobroges row. The page has no infobox; the only area is the Roman-period civitas Viennensium, 'about 13,000 km2' - Isère, Savoie and Haute-Savoie together come to about 19,500 km2 by the gazetteer, within the factor of two. The Cularo (Grenoble) and Vienne oppida lie inside; Lake Geneva is the north-east limit.

ledger.note: 218 BC: the Allobroges, first dated in the sources, as Hannibal crosses their land. Polybius has 'the Allobroges of the plain' helping Hannibal and the mountain Allobroges trying to block him; Vienna had been occupied by Celts since the early 4th century. The page gives no founding date; 218 is the first dated mention (page silent on the origin).

ledger.note: By 130 BC: the Allobroges hold Genaua (Geneva). The page lists '130 BC: Genaua occupied (at the latest)'; it does not say from whom, so the counterpart is 'nobody'.

region.text: Vindalium (Mourre-de-Sève, Sorgues) and the Isère-Rhône confluence near Valence

ledger.note: 121 BC: Domitius Ahenobarbus fights the Allobroges at Vindalium. 'The Battle of Vindalium (121 BC) took place near Vindalium', 'near the oppidum Vindalium (probably Mourre-de-Sève, in Sorgues)'; the Allobroges 'lost 20,000 men, and ... 3,000 of them were captured' (Orosius). Roman campaigns had crossed the Alps from 125 (Allobroges page).

ledger.note: August 121 BC: the Allobroges, Arverni and Saluvii are beaten at the Isère. 'Battle of the Isère River, August 121 BC, where Quintus Fabius Maximus joined the Roman army. Fabius earned the cognomen Allobrogicus.' (The Bituitus page puts it in autumn.)

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria. Pages are thin on geography: no infobox, no area but the Roman-period civitas (13,000 km2); the 218 start is the first dated mention, not a founding. The state ends in 121 to match roman-republic's -121 gain from 'Arverni and Allobroges'; the page says the Allobroges kept autonomy and territory inside the province, so the revolt of Catugnatus (62-61, Ventia taken and Solonion destroyed in 61, ended by Pomptinus) is outside the dossier's life and so not in wars; a gap-filler may prefer a vassal-of-Rome treatment to 61 (the revolt of Catugnatus) or beyond. The land north of the Rhône between Lyon and Geneva (held by the mid-1st century BC) is not drawn. Dates differ: the Allobroges page puts the Isère battle in August 121, the Bituitus page in autumn.
